# Backcasting from AI-Integrated National Cyber Defense Posture: What Policy Coordination Mechanisms Are Missing?

**Problem:** Effective national cyber defense will require coordination between AI labs (who control model access) and government cyber agencies (CISA, NCSC) that doesn't currently exist at the required operational tempo.

**Direction:** Define success state: a national AI cyber defense framework where AI lab capabilities are rapidly deployable for defensive operations with appropriate governance. Work backward: what information sharing agreements, legal authorities, operational protocols, and real-time coordination mechanisms are required? Map gaps against current CISA-industry relationships.

**Why it matters:** The GTG-1002 case showed AI-enabled attacks can operate at machine speed. National cyber defense must respond at similar tempo, requiring pre-built coordination mechanisms rather than ad hoc crisis response.

**Relevant context:** GTG-1002 government targets; CISA AI security guidance; OpenAI Trusted Access government tier; Anthropic Mythos presages speed of attack.
